Why should utilities look at gas and power markets together?
Gas supply, infrastructure and competing sources of demand can all shape the fuel environment facing power markets. For utilities and developers, understanding these dynamics can provide important context for assessing generation economics and developing a long-term power-market strategy. 
Our new infographic, 'From the gas market to the power market', traces four important connections between the gas and power markets: 

Gas supply: how changes in regional production and infrastructure can affect fuel availability and costs for gas-fired generators. 
Pipeline infrastructure: how new capacity and changing gas flows can reshape regional pricing and generation economics.
LNG exports: how growing export demand can compete with domestic gas consumption, particularly where power demand is also increasing.
New power demand: how data centres and other large loads can create new gas demand, infrastructure requirements and considerations around where new gas-fired capacity is commercially viable. 

How can Lens Gas & LNG add context to your power market analysis?
Lens Power & Renewables shows how the power market is evolving. Lens Gas & LNG can add the underlying fuel market context, helping you assess regional production, pipeline development, LNG demand, gas-price outlooks and infrastructure alongside your existing power market analysis.
